messages:
rachael: Quick design check — uploaded a short Figma flow for the rules editor. wondering about the affordances for sorting vs grouping. link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/routing-editor-v2 kevin: saw it, nice. main concern: users keep accidentally dragging rules into groups. need clearer drop targets. :eyes: maria: agree re: drop targets. maybe add an explicit ‘move here’ handle and a subtle snap animation so it’s obvious when a rule will be nested. sam: also keyboard users — can we support ctrl+arrow to reorder and a separate action to nest/unnest? a11y is a must. eli: +1. for keyboard, aria-live notifications would help. e.g., "Rule 3 moved to position 1". shawn: copy nit: when nesting fails due to cycle/loop, message currently says "invalid". can we make it actionable: "Can't nest — this would create a circular rule. Try duplicating or changing priority." rachael: good call on copy. also contrast of the priority chips is low on hover in the left rail — that's been flagged in UX audit. screenshot attached in figma. kevin: quick prototype thought: highlight the exact insertion line with a thin 2px gradient bar and show a small label "Insert between A and B". better than the whole card flash. maria: for mobile/smaller widths, we should avoid dense handles. maybe a long-press to open a mini-menu with Move Up / Move Down / Nest options. sam: question on preview simulation — current simulator uses random sample requests and shows routing order, but I've seen mismatches: preview shows rule order X but runtime logs show Y. could be sorting tie-breaker. eli: that ties into our validation rules: we need a deterministic sort key. if two rules have same priority, fallback should be "created_at" or explicit user order. otherwise preview is misleading. rachael: agreed. propose: 1) UI shows explicit sort criteria in the header (Priority • User order) 2) validation warns when ties exist and suggests explicit reordering. shawn: accessibility items: focus style on cards is invisible on dark theme. keyboard-only users lose context. add a 3px focus ring in theme color and expose aria-describedby with the card's position ("3 of 7"). kevin: dev question — how would we surface the validation errors inline? toast? inline banner? disabled save? maria: inline banners per rule feels best. small red pin icon on the rule with explain-on-hover. saves shouldn't be blocked but we should prevent canary rollout until critical errors are resolved. rachael: agree. UX flows: non-blocking save, block canary if there are unresolved high-severity validation errors. low-severity just shows banner. sam: i'll add keyboard shortcuts doc snippet: ``` // keyboard reordering example Ctrl+Up: move rule up one Ctrl+Down: move rule down one Ctrl+Right: nest under previous rule Ctrl+Left: unnest ``` eli: aria snippet suggestion for the nesting handle: ```html
Rule 3 of 7
``` rachael: solid. final design asks: 1) clearer drop targets + snap animation 2) explicit sort criteria in UI + tie warnings 3) inline per-rule validation banners + non-blocking save 4) keyboard shortcuts + focus ring 5) copy for the circular/nesting error. design-bot: Reminder: design review scheduled tomorrow 11:00am PST. Please add any remaining screen examples to the figma page by EOD. :calendar: kevin: i'll mock the insertion-line variant and test contrast changes. will post updated figma link when done. :zap: maria: i'll draft the copy for the error states and the inline banner microcopy. sam: i'll update the keyboard shortcuts doc and add unit tests for deterministic sort. rachael: thanks all — will collate and follow up with a PR checklist for engineering. :thumbsup:
